figures.title: The score matrix as causal tiles that never leave the chip
figures.caption: FlashAttention computes attention one Br x Bc score tile at a time. A Q tile of 128 rows is 32 KB, a K tile of 64 columns is 16 KB, and the score tile is 16 KB; with the matching V tile the working set is 80 KB. The L x L matrix is never written to HBM, so the 20 GB per head per layer is never materialized.
figures.alt: A ten-by-ten grid of tiles. Row i has a live S tile in every column up to i and blank cells after it, so the live tiles form a lower triangle under the causal mask. The last row is highlighted. Each cell is one 128-by-64 score tile built in shared memory, softmaxed with a running max, multiplied by its V tile, and accumulated; blank cells are masked and never computed.

data.note: Schematic 10 x 10 tile map. In deployment Br = 128 and Bc = 64, so the real tile grid is far larger than shown. Blank cells are masked by causality and never computed.

anim.intro: Walk one Q tile across its K/V tiles.

steps.label: Load one Q tile of Br = 128 rows and one K tile of Bc = 64 columns into shared memory.
Compute the 128 x 64 score tile; it stays in registers and shared memory.
Fold the tile into the running max m and sum l; rescale the accumulator by alpha = exp(m_old - m_new).
Multiply by the matching V tile and accumulate the Br x d output block.
Advance to the next K tile; the L x L matrix never exists.

figures.title: What fits in one SM's shared memory
figures.caption: One 128 x 64 stage needs 80 KB: a 32 KB Q tile, 16 KB each for K, V, and the score tile. Double-buffering K and V brings the resident set to 112 KB, which fits Hopper's 228 KB per SM and Ampere's 164 KB, leaving 116 KB free on Hopper.
figures.alt: A memory strip of 228 KB. The Q tile takes 32 KB, K takes 16 KB, V takes 16 KB, the score tile takes 16 KB, and the double buffers K-prime and V-prime take 16 KB each, for 112 KB used. The remaining 116 KB is free headroom.

data.note: K, V, S, K-prime, and V-prime are 16 KB each. One stage is 80 KB; double-buffered K and V make 112 KB. Hopper allows 228 KB per SM, Ampere 164 KB, so the 112 KB resident set leaves 116 KB free on Hopper.

figures.title: The score matrix is 390 times the keys and values it summarizes
figures.caption: At L = 100,000 and d_head = 128, storing one head's score matrix takes L^2 x 2 bytes = 20 GB, while its keys and values take 4Ld bytes = 51.2 MB. The ratio is L / 2d = 390x, and in FP32 the matrix would be 40 GB. FlashAttention stores none of it and recomputes the tiles in the backward pass for 2.56e12 extra FLOPs.
figures.alt: Two horizontal bars. The score matrix for one head is 20 GB, L squared times two bytes. The keys and values for the same head are 51.2 MB, four times L times d bytes, a sliver beside the matrix. The ratio between them is 390 to 1.

data.note: The 20 GB bar is L^2 x 2 bytes; 51.2 MB is 4Ld. At 262,144 positions the keys and values for one head are 262,144 × 128 × 2 × 2 = 134.2 MB, while a stored score matrix would be 262,144 × 262,144 × 2 = 137.4 GB, nearly seven times the 20 GB at L = 100,000.
